source.label: A lower bound for the Gram form's negative part on the binomial family, and the family's visibility behind a lattice of bounded constant

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: Setting of the binomial cluster form bound: complete grid, flat window, bandwidth L, the family of k + 1 off-axis pairs at distance delta, heights gamma_0 + j pi/L, multiplicities binom(k, j), b = delta L, B the off-axis part of the form, K(S) = (2 cos(pi S/2L))^k 2 cosh(delta S), gamma_c = gamma_0 + k pi/(2L). (1) For every real odd o in L^2[-L/2, L/2], not zero, the vector u of f(t) = i e^{i gamma_c t} o(t) is real and u^T B u/|u|^2 = -(1/(L ||o||^2)) iint o(t) o(t') K(t + t') dt dt'. (2) If k >= 1, b >= 4(k+1), b^2 >= (4 pi^2/3) k (k+1)^2 and e^b >= 6e 2^(k+2) (k+1) e^(2k+2) (b/pi)^k/k!, then lambda_min(B) <= -(1/(12e)) (2 e^b/b) k! (pi/b)^k. (3) Under the conditions of (2), with a lattice of real points of spacing s <= 2 pi/L and multiplicity one, the whole form has a negative eigenvalue whenever 2 pi/(sL) < (1/(12e)) (2 e^b/b) k! (pi/b)^k, in particular whenever 2 pi/(sL) < (1/(6e b)) e^(b(1 - 1/pi)). (4) For the same points in the form at bandwidth 2L, off-axis part B': if b >= 3.4 and b^2 >= 4 pi^2 k then lambda_min(B') <= -0.1 2^k e^(2b)/b.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof: with the phase e^{i gamma_c t} the family's exponential sum becomes the nonnegative kernel K, the form at f is minus a double integral of o o' K, and for o made of an exponential of rate delta/(k+1) at each end, cut at width 2(k+1)/delta, the two ends' own terms exceed twice their cross term under the three conditions; the test function is a reviewer's. With the upper bound on record this fixes the smallest eigenvalue within the factor 12e in that range. In eleven instances inside the range the form at the test function is 0.29 to 0.32 of the upper bound and the smallest eigenvalue 0.30 to 0.34. At twice the bandwidth the kernel's factor has modulus 2^k at the endpoint, and a test function at the two ends, odd or even with the parity of k, gives part (4); in ten instances the smallest eigenvalue there is 0.96 to 0.99 of one pair's with the total multiplicity. One family, one spacing; k proportional to b is outside the range.
claims.rationale: At a bandwidth c log T with c <= 1, fixed distance and a lattice of the zeros' density, the three conditions hold for every multiplicity 2^k up to a multiple of log T once T is large, and the binomial family is then visible to the form in the model; the family's hiding, on record for short bandwidths, does not persist there. One family on the complete grid; distances shrinking with T and c > 1 are not covered.
claims.next_action: None planned; the range of b between a constant and k log b, and c > 1, are open.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; the identity of (1) and the bound of (2) hold numerically in eleven instances, the identity by two computations that do not share its derivation.
notes.significance: Context: completes a model statement in the range the goal's instances need. No novelty claimed.
notes.relationships: The lower bound matching the binomial cluster form bound's upper bound; uses its parts (1) and (4).

relationships: Part (1) of that proposition gives the form at a vector as a double integral, and its part (4) the lattice's constant.
The same family; on record as hidden from the diagonal at bandwidths up to about 1.47 times the logarithm of the density over delta.

That proposition gives the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the off-axis part for any cluster at one distance, asymptotically for fixed k; this one is a lower bound for the smallest eigenvalue of one family with explicit conditions. Neither is stated so as to imply the other.
The case of one pair, where the smallest eigenvalue is about -m(kappa - 1).
